title: Illinois's 9th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Illinois's 9th Congressional District is an open-seat race following the retirement of longtime Democratic incumbent Jan Schakowsky, who represented the district for 14 terms. The district covers parts of Chicago's North Side and northern suburbs including Evanston, Skokie, and Arlington Heights, and is rated as a safely Democratic seat by major election forecasters. The Democratic primary was a competitive 16-candidate field won by Evanston Mayor and former state legislator Daniel Biss. Biss will face Republican nominee John Elleson, a pastor who previously ran for the seat in 2018, and independent candidate Delila Barrera, a behavioral technician and activist, in the November general election.
polling_note: No general election polling was found for this race; only Democratic primary polls (conducted by Global Strategy Group and Lester & Associates in late 2025) were available, which are not applicable to the general election.

candidates.name: Daniel K. Biss
candidates.summary: Daniel Biss is the mayor of Evanston, Illinois, and the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 9th Congressional District. A former mathematician and University of Chicago professor, he previously served in the Illinois House of Representatives and Illinois Senate, and was a candidate for governor in 2018. Biss won a competitive 16-candidate Democratic primary in March 2026 to succeed retiring incumbent Jan Schakowsky.

Elleson won the Republican primary in March 2026 and campaigns on a platform of fiscal responsibility, bipartisan immigration reform, and community service.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, which constrains confidence. However, the district profile (Chicago's North Side, Evanston, Skokie, Arlington Heights) is described by major forecasters as safely Democratic. The seat was held for 14 terms by a Democrat, and the open-seat contest follows retirement, not a partisan shift. Democratic nominee Daniel Biss—Evanston mayor, former state legislator, and winner of a 16-candidate primary—faces Republican John Elleson, who lost the same district by a wide margin in 2018, and independent Delila Barrera, whose profile does not suggest a competitive challenge. The district's strong Democratic baseline and the candidates' relative strength support an overwhelming Democratic advantage despite the polling gap.
